newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa at two-week low as rally fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa at two-week low as rally fizzles out.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures tumbled to a two-week low as weak long holders liquidated their positions built up during a rally over the past weeks, traders said on Thursday.
"The longs are wrong and are getting out," said one.
By midsession, benchmark September lost 3.5 percent or 39 stg on the day to stand at 1,070 stg a tonne.
It gapped 22 stg down at the open, and well below its previous key chart support at 1,110, after another sharp slide in New York overnight on spec long liquidation.
Values then managed to consolidate at between the day's range of between 1,064 and 1,087.

Traders also saw the sharp reversal as a correction to the recent dazzling rally, which had hoisted prices to one-year highs. "It's a technical correction here until the new fundamental inputs are in."
This week alone, the market had lost some nine percent in value.
Volume was brisk at 5,622 lots, centred on September and December contracts. Options volume was meagre at 65 lots.
Traders pegged initial support at around mid-1,040s basis September ahead of the breakaway gap at 1,046 and 1,059. Resistance is seen at the previous support at 1,100.
"But the firm sterling will inhibit the market from taking off," said one trader.

The strong pound could encourage origin selling but except for some belated hedge selling, origins were well sold. But at the same time, it would deter buying by manufacturers, who had picked up some cocoa during the recent run-up.

Cocoa's rally since mid-June was fuelled by aggressive fund-led and industry buying amid an improved chart picture and the longer-term adverse impact of the El Nino weather pattern on future harvests.

In overnight news, mid-crop cocoa arrivals from Ivory Coast looked set to increase from late July. Arrivals totalled 50,000 tonnes from end-June but still had the potential to reach 150,000 by end-August.
Europe's second-quarter cocoa grind figures, due on Friday or early next week, were expected to show a mixed trend.
The New York market is closed on Friday for the Independence Day holiday. Traders said the market could gap $35 down on Thursday and there could be further spec long liquidation.
